LESSON: READING 3.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should we read extensively?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. explain vocabulary related to the theme for effective communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading

Teach
• Focus skill: explain vocabulary related to the theme for effective communication.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read extensively?
2. Why is it important to take care of wildlife?
3. What can be done to avoid road accidents involving wild animals?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
